label: John 11:1
text: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha.

label: John 11:2
text: It was that Mary who had anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother, Lazarus, was sick.

label: John 11:3
text: The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, “Lord, behold, he for whom you have great affection is sick.”

label: John 11:4
text:
But when Jesus heard it, he said,
“This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God, that God’s Son may be glorified by it.”

label: John 11:5
text: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

label: John 11:6
text: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.

label: John 11:7
text:
Then after this he said to the disciples,
“Let’s go into Judea again.”

label: John 11:8
text: The disciples told him, “Rabbi, the Jews were just trying to stone you, and are you going there again?”

label: John 11:9
text:
Jesus answered,
“Aren’t there twelve hours of daylight? If a man walks in the day, he doesn’t stumble, because he sees the light of this world.

label: John 11:10
text: But if a man walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light isn’t in him.”

label: John 11:11
text:
He said these things, and after that, he said to them,
“Our friend, Lazarus, has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I may awake him out of sleep.”

label: John 11:12
text: The disciples therefore said, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover.”

label: John 11:13
text: Now Jesus had spoken of his death, but they thought that he spoke of taking rest in sleep.

label: John 11:14
text:
So Jesus said to them plainly then,
“Lazarus is dead.

label: John 11:15
text: I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, so that you may believe. Nevertheless, let’s go to him.”

label: John 11:16
text: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let’s go also, that we may die with him.”

label: John 11:17
text: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.

label: John 11:18
text: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.

label: John 11:19
text: Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.

label: John 11:20
text: Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.

label: John 11:21
text: Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.

label: John 11:22
text: Even now I know that, whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”

label: John 11:23
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Your brother will rise again.”

label: John 11:24
text: Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

label: John 11:25
text:
Jesus said to her,
“I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.

label: John 11:26
text: Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”

label: John 11:27
text: She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world.”

label: John 11:28
text: When she had said this, she went away, and called Mary, her sister, secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here, and is calling you.”

label: John 11:29
text: When she heard this, she arose quickly, and went to him.

label: John 11:30
text: Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was in the place where Martha met him.

label: John 11:31
text: Then the Jews who were with her in the house, and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.”

label: John 11:32
text: Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.”

label: John 11:33
text: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,

label: John 11:34
text:
and said,
“Where have you laid him?”
They told him, “Lord, come and see.”

label: John 11:35
text: Jesus wept.

label: John 11:36
text: The Jews therefore said, “See how much affection he had for him!”

label: John 11:37
text: Some of them said, “Couldn’t this man, who opened the eyes of him who was blind, have also kept this man from dying?”

label: John 11:38
text: Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.

label: John 11:39
text:
Jesus said,
“Take away the stone.”
Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”

label: John 11:40
text:
Jesus said to her,
“Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?”

label: John 11:41
text:
So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said,
“Father, I thank you that you listened to me.

label: John 11:42
text: I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”

label: John 11:43
text:
When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice,
“Lazarus, come out!”

label: John 11:44
text:
He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth.
Jesus said to them,
“Free him, and let him go.”

label: John 11:45
text: Therefore many of the Jews, who came to Mary and saw what Jesus did, believed in him.

label: John 11:46
text: But some of them went away to the Pharisees, and told them the things which Jesus had done.

label: John 11:47
text: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, “What are we doing? For this man does many signs.

label: John 11:48
text: If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”

label: John 11:49
text: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all,

label: John 11:50
text: nor do you consider that it is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish.”

label: John 11:51
text: Now he didn’t say this of himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation,

label: John 11:52
text: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God who are scattered abroad.

label: John 11:53
text: So from that day forward they took counsel that they might put him to death.

label: John 11:54
text: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed from there into the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim. He stayed there with his disciples.

label: John 11:55
text: Now the Passover of the Jews was at hand. Many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves.

label: John 11:56
text: Then they sought for Jesus and spoke one with another, as they stood in the temple, “What do you think—that he isn’t coming to the feast at all?”

label: John 11:57
text: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, that they might seize him.

label: Lazarus of Bethany was sick
statement: Lazarus of Bethany, the brother of Mary and Martha, was sick.
note: Luke 10 knows Martha and Mary but not Lazarus and does not name their village.

label: Mary of Bethany anointed the Lord with ointment
statement: Mary of Bethany anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair.
note: A back-reference anticipating John 12:3; John names the woman, Matthew 26:6-13 leaves her unnamed.

label: The Jews had recently tried to stone Jesus
statement: The disciples say the Jews in Jerusalem had recently tried to stone Jesus.

label: The daylight was reckoned as twelve hours
statement: Daylight was reckoned as twelve hours ('Aren't there twelve hours of daylight?').

label: Thomas is called Didymus
statement: Thomas, one of the Twelve, was called Didymus, meaning 'the twin'.

label: Lazarus had been in the tomb four days
statement: When Jesus arrived at Bethany, Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days.

label: Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away
statement: Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia (roughly 2.4-2.8 km) away.

label: Many Jews came to console Martha and Mary
statement: Many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother: mourners gathered at the house of the bereaved in the Jerusalem area.

label: Martha believes in the resurrection at the last day
statement: Martha expressed belief that her brother would rise again 'in the resurrection at the last day'.

label: The mourners followed Mary to the tomb to weep
statement: The mourners sitting with Mary in the house followed her when she rose quickly, supposing she was going to the tomb to weep there.

label: Jesus had opened the eyes of a man born blind
statement: Some of the mourners say this man had opened the eyes of a man who was blind.
note: A back-reference to John 9, where the man is blind from birth.

label: The tomb was a cave with a stone across it
statement: Lazarus's tomb was a cave with a stone lying against its entrance.

label: Jesus raised Lazarus by calling him from the tomb
statement: Jesus cried with a loud voice 'Lazarus, come out!', and the dead man came out of the tomb, bound with wrappings.
note: Miracle claim: recorded none-found after honest searching; setting evidence never attests the miracle.

label: The chief priests and Pharisees gathered a council
statement: The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council (Sanhedrin) and asked what to do, 'for this man does many signs'.
note: John places this council after the raising of Lazarus, before the final week; Matthew 26:3 gathers the leaders two days before the Passover.

label: The council feared the Romans would take away their place and nation
statement: The council feared that if everyone believed in Jesus, the Romans would come and take away both their place and their nation.
note: The fear is the claim. The destruction of Jerusalem in 70 CE is the later event and is never evidence that the prediction was fulfilled.

label: Caiaphas was high priest 'that year'
statement: Caiaphas was high priest 'that year', at the time of the council.
note: John repeats the phrase 'high priest that year' (11:49, 51); Josephus dates the tenure to about 18-36 CE.

label: Jesus withdrew to the city called Ephraim
statement: Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews but went to the country near the wilderness, to the city called Ephraim, and stayed there with his disciples.

label: Many went up before the Passover to purify themselves
statement: At the Passover of the Jews, many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves.

label: The leaders ordered that Jesus's whereabouts be reported
statement: The chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where Jesus was, he should report it, so that they might seize him.
